en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ambayāgadāyaka Udakāsanavagga 8 I gave a mango fruit to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was free from all defilements. Because of that deed, I have attained the fruit of Stream-entry (*sotāpatti-phala*). Having reached the state of a Stream-enterer, I am now free from rebirth in the lower realms. I shall attain final Nibbāna before long; this is my last birth. I have seen the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One. I have heard the Dhamma, which is well-expounded by the Teacher. I have entered the Order of the Well-Gone One (*Sugata-sāsana*). I have become one who has crossed over the flood and reached the further shore. I have attained the fruit of Stream-entry; I am no longer subject to rebirth in the states of misery. I am a Stream-enterer, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms. I shall attain final Nibbāna before long; this is my last birth. That gift which I gave back in the ninety-first aeon—
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of the offering of mangoes.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Ambayāgadāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Ambayāgadāyaka is the eighth.
